question: Describe balancing urgent operational work with important longer-term or strategic work.

raiseTranscript.text: Describe balancing urgent operational work with important longer-term or strategic work.

In my last project I had daily ticket triage plus a side task to document our onboarding process. I blocked two hours every morning for tickets and used the afternoon for the doc after checking with my mentor on priorities.
How did you decide what to push when both felt urgent?
I asked my manager which one had the bigger risk if delayed a day, then moved the doc work to the next sprint when tickets spiked.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe balancing urgent operational work with important longer-term or strategic work.

junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. The story shows the candidate owns their own schedule and seeks guidance on trade-offs rather than guessing. Quote about asking for risk assessment demonstrates coachability. Scope stays individual and local, which matches level. Biggest strength is the explicit check-in habit; biggest gap is lack of any forward planning beyond the current week.

I moved two migration tasks to the partner team and documented the decision in the shared doc so the delay was explicit rather than hidden.

How did you handle underperformance on the strategic track?
One engineer kept deprioritizing the rewrite. I paired them with a stronger peer for two sprints and made the rewrite deliverables part of their quarterly goals.

raiseTranscript.text: Describe balancing urgent operational work with important longer-term or strategic work.

Our org faced constant incidents while trying to move to a new architecture. I set an org-wide rule that 25% of every team's capacity must go to the new platform, created a central triage team to absorb spikes, and tied the architecture milestones to the annual operating plan reviewed by the CFO.
How did you handle the first quarter when incidents still consumed more than expected?
I delayed two product launches by six weeks and publicly reset the architecture timeline in the all-hands so the trade-off was visible at the company level.
